item.title: Preserving Utility in Continual LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Projections
item.description:
This research tackles the problem of repeatedly removing sensitive data from a large language model without losing performance. The authors built Continual Orthogonal Projection (COP), a simple gradient‑projection method that keeps each deletion orthogonal to previous ones, so utility stays high and forgetting stays strong. Experiments on standard benchmarks show COP outperforms existing continual‑unlearning techniques.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud‑hosted LLMs, here is what to do: 1) add COP’s low‑rank basis cache to your inference pipeline; 2) whenever a deletion request arrives, run a single gradient step constrained to COP’s orthogonal subspace; 3) monitor utility metrics to confirm no drift. If your org uses continual data deletion, check that your current unlearning routine isn’t causing interference between successive requests.

item.title: [News] AI can make tech CEOs’ lives easier. What about everyone else?
item.description: TechCrunch reports that several high-profile AI CEOs have made remarks highlighting AI’s role in everyday life, sparking criticism that these leaders may be out of touch with ordinary users. The piece underscores a broader industry debate on how AI marketing and product positioning might alienate non-technical audiences.

item.title: [News] Chatbots Are Leading Hikers Astray, With Dangerous Consequences
item.description: Google Gemini and Anthropic Claude chatbots have been cited as contributing factors in several backcountry hiking accidents, leading to misnavigation and dangerous decision-making by users.

item.title: [News] Apple CEO says the company doesn’t ‘want to ship AI for AI’s sake’
item.description: Apple CEO John Ternus stated that Apple will not ship AI simply for its own sake, focusing instead on meaningful, user‑centered AI integration in future products. The comment reflects Apple’s cautious approach to AI deployment across its ecosystem.

item.title: [News] 4 days left: How TechCrunch Founder Summit helps you make more useful connections to scale
item.description: TechCrunch Founder Summit in Boston offers a structured networking platform powered by Braindate, enabling attendees to schedule targeted one-on-one and small-group conversations on specific topics. The event aims to replace random networking with intentional, topic-driven connections and continued engagement beyond the venue.

item.title: [News] Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward
item.description: A federal judge has allowed the NAACP lawsuit to proceed against xAI, a SpaceX-owned AI company, over alleged violations of the Clean Air Act for operating unpermitted combustion turbines at its Colossus data center.
